items.reasoning: Cloud computing is on-demand compute/storage/network delivered over the internet from provider-operated capacity; colocation, shared hosting and on-prem virtualization are not.
Under PaaS the customer always keeps information/data and accounts/identities; OS, runtime/middleware and physical security sit with the provider.
Single-tenant dedicated environment is a private cloud regardless of whether a third party hosts and operates the facility.
Records legally pinned on-premises plus a seasonal public burst is the textbook hybrid pattern.
Consumption-based means no upfront purchase, charges tracking actual use, and a bill that falls when usage stops.
Selling owned hardware and renting monthly services is precisely the CapEx-to-OpEx shift.
Flat, continuous, predictable 24/7 load is the canonical reserved-term case; spot suits interruptible work, not a core ledger.
Checkpointed, resumable, deadline-free batch is the canonical interruptible/spot-capacity workload.
Serverless removes infrastructure duties but never the customer's code, its configuration and its data.
High availability = redundant components so the service survives a component failure, expressed as an uptime target; backup and monitoring are different concerns.
A 45x burst within minutes then shrink back is horizontal scale-out/in; a vertical resize cannot elastically meet that shape.
Reliability is recovering from failure and continuing; predictability is knowing performance and cost in advance - option A is the same pair swapped.
The security benefit is inherited platform capability (policy, patch currency, network protection), not a transfer of accountability.
Manageability = administering the estate remotely through the platform's own tooling and automation.
In IaaS the customer owns the guest OS and everything above it; the provider owns physical hosts, storage, network and hypervisor.
Developers writing their own app with nobody on OS/runtime/middleware is the PaaS definition; SaaS would mean not writing it at all.
Licensing a finished product and configuring only features and users is SaaS - least responsibility and least control.

Finished product configured by seats = SaaS; vendor-pinned OS patch level the customer must control = IaaS; deploy custom code with no runtime/middleware duty = PaaS; licensed ready-to-use accounting = SaaS.
A region is a set of datacenters on a low-latency network; region pairs sit at distance for replication and receive updates sequentially, not simultaneously.
A sovereign region is a nationally isolated Azure instance with its own boundary for government/residency obligations, not a customer-built private cloud.
Surviving loss of a whole datacenter including power and cooling needs availability zones; availability sets only protect within one datacenter.
A resource belongs to exactly one resource group, and resources may live in regions other than their group's location.
The subscription is the billing and access boundary; multiple subscriptions can trust a single Entra tenant so identities stay shared.
Management groups sit above subscriptions and inherit assignments to current and future subscriptions - least ongoing effort at forty subscriptions.
Custom OS configuration = VM, portable packaged image = container, event-triggered snippet = Functions.
Identical instances whose count rises and falls automatically is the Virtual Machine Scale Sets definition; availability sets do not change instance count.
A VM cannot exist without an OS managed disk and a NIC attached to a virtual network; public IP, Bastion and availability set are optional (and a public IP is excluded here).
Push code and let the platform run OS, patching and web plumbing, without adopting images, is the managed web app (App Service) option.
A virtual network is isolated by default, its subnets route to each other automatically, and Azure DNS is an Azure resource managed like any other.
Constant traffic with predictable latency and no public-internet path is exactly ExpressRoute's private circuit; VPN options ride the internet.
A private endpoint gives the service a private address inside the VNet reached over the Microsoft backbone, allowing public access to be disabled.
Massive unstructured objects = Blob; SMB/UNC shared drive = Files; persistent volume attached to a VM = Disk; small transient messages = Queue; large write-once binary exports = Blob.
Tier choice follows access frequency over the data's lifetime - hot while read constantly, then cool/archive - not the data's importance.
Redundancy should match replaceability: regenerable telemetry can drop to LRS while irreplaceable contract records stay geo-redundant.
Continuous synchronization between an on-premises Windows file server and Azure Files is Azure File Sync; AzCopy and Storage Explorer are one-off transfer tools.
900 TB against a 40 TB window is the offline case - physically ship Data Box appliances.
Legacy domain-join and older domain protocols without running domain controllers is Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
Proving who you are (password plus one-time code) is authentication; deciding what you may see (own branch only) is authorization.
External identities / B2B collaboration lets partners work using accounts they already own, with no account creation in the host tenant.
Conditional Access evaluates signals such as device state and location at sign-in and requires an extra control before granting access.
Azure RBAC assignments are additive and inherited downward: Reader over the subscription plus Contributor on one group yields read everywhere, write in that group.

Zero Trust's own principles are verify explicitly and least-privilege/just-in-time access; trusted internal network and a doubled perimeter are the model it replaces, and layered defence is defence-in-depth.

Posture assessment plus threat protection plus regulatory compliance is Microsoft Defender for Cloud - but option C is that product's own former name, so I am picking on current canonical vocabulary rather than on a clean conceptual separation.
Deallocation stops compute metering only: provisioned managed disks and a reserved public IP keep billing on their own meters.
Reads crossing a region boundary all day is outbound data transfer, which meters on its own line; ingress and resource groups are not billed.
Estimating a not-yet-deployed workload's monthly cost from proposed services, sizes and regions is the pricing calculator; cost analysis only reads charges already incurred.
Explaining charges already incurred by resource, service and date is cost analysis.
Being warned while spend climbs toward an agreed ceiling is a budget with consumption alerts.
Tags carry cost attribution across resource groups that do not match the reporting dimension, and cost reports group by tag without rebuilding the estate.
Discovering, mapping, classifying and tracking data as it moves is Microsoft Purview; Defender for Cloud handles infrastructure posture, which the stem excludes.
Refusing non-compliant deployments at creation time is Azure Policy with an allowed-locations rule; locks block deletion or change, not region choice.
Azure Policy evaluates existing resources for compliance state as well as denying future non-compliant deployments - one control answers both asks.
A delete lock refuses deletion for every principal, including owners, until the lock is deliberately removed.
Region restriction and mandatory tag enforcement are Azure Policy; delete protection above owner rights is a resource lock; read-but-not-change is an RBAC role assignment.
The portal's strength is visual exploration and ad-hoc inspection; repetitive builds and bulk changes belong in code or CLI, and screenshots are not a definition.
Nothing installed, no stored credentials, already signed in to the browser is Azure Cloud Shell.
Inventorying and governing on-premises and other-cloud servers with Azure tooling, without moving them, is Azure Arc.
IaC buys repeatable identical deployments from one declaration and a versioned, reviewable artifact; it does not remove approvals, transfer responsibility, or self-heal drift unattended.
Portal, CLI and scripts all submit to Azure Resource Manager, the single control plane where RBAC and policy are enforced.
Personalized, prioritized recommendations across cost, security, reliability and operations derived from the actual estate is Azure Advisor.
Service Health is subscription-scoped platform incident and maintenance reporting; the public status page is not scoped, and resource health covers one resource.
One platform collecting and correlating metrics and logs across the whole estate and acting on them is Azure Monitor; Log Analytics and Application Insights are parts of it.
Interrogating already-collected log data interactively and refining the query is Log Analytics.
Threshold detection plus automatic remediation is an Azure Monitor alert rule with an action; dashboards and scheduled reads are human-in-the-loop.
Infrastructure metrics are normal but in-application requests and page usage are in question - that is Application Insights.
